research_rationale: EO 14177 (January 23, 2025, 90 FR 8643, Federal Register FR Doc. 2025-02121) established the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) in section 2, set its membership and co-chairs, gave it advisory functions including service as the President's Innovation and Technology Advisory Committee and the National Nanotechnology Advisory Panel (section 3), provided for administration by the Department of Energy and for clearances, subcommittees and unpaid service (section 4), set its term at two years unless extended (section 5), revoked EO 14007 (section 6) and added general provisions (section 7). I read the held Federal Register text layer of the whole order (verified whole-order span, three PDF pages) and confirm the dossier inventory of 25 scopes: the lead-in, sections 1 to 7 and their lettered and numbered subparts, with nothing omitted. Sections 2 to 5 and 7 are operative on 2026-10-14. The two-year term in section 5 would end on 2027-01-23 on its own terms, after the cutoff, and EO 14354 of September 29, 2025 (90 FR 48145, effective September 30, 2025) continues PCAST, listed in its section 1(u) with this order cited, until September 30, 2027. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order in full as a note to 42 U.S.C. 6601 without any revocation or amendment annotation. Section 6, the revocation of EO 14007 (as amended by EO 14109), was a self-executing act performed on signing and is recorded as terminated on 2025-01-23. Bounded searches: current-law:usc found the 42 U.S.C. 6601 note (its edition runs through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted on 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 would not appear; none is suggested by any held source); current-law:ecfr has no hit; later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25) lists EO 14177 as revoking EO 14007, 'Continued by: EO 14354, September 29, 2025', and as 'See' EO 12968 and EO 14009. The EO 12968 reference is the order's own section 4(c) citation of that clearance order. The 'EO 14009, September 29, 2023' entry carries the date of EO 14109 (the order amending EO 14007 that section 6 itself names); the held text of EO 14009 (86 FR 7793, January 28, 2021) is Strengthening Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act and does not mention PCAST or this order. No held order revokes, supersedes or amends EO 14177.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause for the order it revokes. Section 6 revoked EO 14007 outright on signing, and section 7(a) only preserves the authority of departments and agencies and the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; section 7(c) disclaims any enforceable right or benefit. No right, appointment or proceeding under EO 14007 is preserved by any term of EO 14177, and no held source shows one.
earlier_end_check: No end on or before 2026-10-14. Own terms: section 5 terminates PCAST two years from January 23, 2025 (2027-01-23, whether the end is read as inclusive or exclusive), unless extended by the President; that date is after the cutoff, and EO 14354 (effective 2025-09-30) continues PCAST until September 30, 2027. Later orders: a search of the held corpus for the number finds it only in copies of EO 14354 (a continuation, not an end) and copies of EO 14177 itself; the OFR catalog shows no revocation, supersession or amendment. Statute: no repeal or expiry of an authority is involved, because the order rests on the President's constitutional and statutory authority generally and the Federal Advisory Committee Act treatment is set by section 4(f) and EO 14354 section 2.
scope_check: The inventory covers the lead-in (authority recital), section 1 (purpose), section 2 (establishment, membership, co-chairs), section 3 (functions and the two statutory designations), section 4 (administration, subparts (a) to (f)), section 5 (termination), section 6 (revocation) and section 7 (general provisions). The scope ids sec3-i to sec3-i-iv are items (i) to (iv) of section 3(b); sec7-i and sec7-i-ii are items (i) and (ii) of section 7(a). Page-break text (VerDate lines and the PDF page headers) sits inside the spans of sec3, sec4 and sec7-i; it is not operative text.
independent_command_check: Each clause is a separate command or statement: the establishment (sec. 2(a)), composition (2(b)), co-chairs (2(c)), advisory function (3(a)), the four duties of 3(b) (i) to (iv), advice to the NSTC (3(c)), agency information duty (4(a)), subcommittee authority (4(b)), clearance authority (4(c)), Department of Energy support (4(d)), compensation rule (4(e)), Federal Advisory Committee Act functions (4(f)), the term (5), the revocation (6) and the construction clauses (7). Only the revocation in section 6 was performed once; the others continue while PCAST exists, so the end of one does not end the others. Section 4(f) and EO 14354 section 2 assign the same Federal Advisory Committee Act functions to the Department of Energy; EO 14354 does not say it replaces section 4(f), so section 4(f) is recorded as continuing with EO 14354 as a later event.
savings_check: No savings clause, partial revocation or exempting provision is in the order. The only revocation (section 6) is complete. EO 14354 has its own general provisions and does not limit EO 14177. Nothing in the 2026-10-28 evidence ruling lets a later general rule end these commands, and none was found.
